english: Among the tangled mess of vines and mossy rocks, you see the thick roots of a Brachen tree. They crack open the walls and ceiling of this half-dwarven, half-antesepalian chamber.
It spreads like a thousand-footed spider.
M-So this is the bottom of the big tree.
They are soft on the surface. A layer of moss.
Alas, I don't think it's got a mouth. Or a brain.
I guess you could talk to it with some magic. Then again, I'm no expert.
They are thick, and create a vast, tight forest.
There might be something there. Hidden beyond the wall of roots.
The roots go deeper. Much, much deeper.
The many, many roots of the Brachen tree fill the chamber.
(Nod your head and stop speaking to the tree.)
It would be a good display of your might.
It would be difficult. The tree is ancient and powerful.
There is clearly something hidden inside here.
While brute force is a bit passé... it might be suitable here.
You walk over to them- each root dangling before you like a tendril of foul ideologies.
(Scream, a Primal yell, and grab the roots.)
Before you can put any type of power into it, the tree reacts.
You walk over to grab the roots - and start pulling.
With a forceful yank, the roots... don't seem to move an inch.
However, the muscles in your back seem to do so.
You need help, Cleric? Want me to call someone?
Your muscles are pulsating in pain.
The entire back is messed up now.
You hear a roar coming from further down the chamber.
Quiet! No yelling by the Roots!
She's right. Don't make so much noise. It's beneath a man of your stature.
The roots are very firm and rigid.
You cannot break them like this. Or at least it is very unlikely.
Maybe you can try something else, Cleric. Have you asked the tree nicely?
The roots slowly, but ever so slightly widen, revealing the goods within.
Lord Puu appears to allow you to loot its cache now.
It clearly could not stand your might.
You touch the surface of the tree. The soft moss dampens your glove. Then you trace a spiral with your index finger.
The primal magic causes the roots to stir. A deep rumble shoots through the chamber.
One of the roots reaches out. Towards you.
Is it hostile? I mean... doesn't feel like it.
You step out of the way.
The tendril misses you, instead slowly waving in the air where your head was a second ago.
As you do, the entire root system begins to shake.
The root is pulled back, out of your hand.
The root slowly reaches for the top of your helm.
The goblin takes a step back and clears his throat.
I'll let you handle this. Making friends with trees isn't really my thing.
The voice is wind. Faintly rushing through moss and stone.
A smell of wet stagnant ponds and moldy basements fills your nose.
The tree appears to... growl. Then it goes silent.
He nods and takes another small step back. "Okay. Right."
Then, after several more seconds of nothing but faint wind emanating from the roots - it SPEAKS.
...FOR YOU. TO SPEAK. WITH THE LORD... OF THE EARTH.
Sure. I have some questions for you, Lord Puu.
A great honor indeed. (Bow your head.)
Right. Anyway, answer my question, tree.
The tree lets out a moldy wind. It envelops you.
Why do you speak so slowly? Is that a tree-thing?
What are you voting in the election, Lord Puu?
What do you do here all day?
Do you have a permit to root here, tree?
It does not respond at first.
Or is it an age-thing? I'm assuming you get slow with time. At least us humans do.
Okay, that's fair. Sorry for asking so many questions.
Get used to it, buddy boy.
Right. Uh... I have some other questions.
The wind turns yet again into a growl.
The tree knows the smartest way, clearly.
Do you want to know what I'm voting for?
The tree is silent, but for the faint wind.
Just like that? You're not gonna offer your opinion anyway?
...Right. But everyone else is just dying to hear your thoughts.
Then the wind slowly turns into a voice again, letting out a single word.
However the tree interpreted the word hustle, it must not have been too worrisome.
Who exactly offered you a permit?
The roots just nod towards you. Then the voice repeats.
His logic is that he owns the land he was planted on.
Self-sustaining and natural. Of course he owns his land.
That's not good. He might catch a cold.
He's saying he would rather not.
Oh. It is a bit cold down here, but I'm not asking about that.
He takes another little step back.
The goblin gives you a casual shrug.
THE GREEN WITCH OF THE WATER BELOW. SHE IS TRUE BEAUTY.
AS DEW UPON THE LEAVES OF A SUNSET'S HOTNESS.
Okay, I think I've heard enough.
The tree's voice turns into whistling winds.
The tree appears to agree with you wholeheartedly.
You whisper to yourself the words to pull the Strings around the mossy bark.
Go now. You should not be waking...
With that, the voice turns to wind, and then the wind turns to silence in the chamber.
Interesting chat. I like that spell though. The fact that I can hear your little conversation makes me feel so included. It's great.
